cards.front: Secondary PPH (24 hours to 6 weeks postpartum) is most commonly due to retained products of conception or [___]; investigate with pelvic ultrasound.
cards.context:
Retained placental tissue and endometritis (infection of the uterine lining) can prevent normal uterine involution, causing bleeding 24 hours to 6 weeks after birth.

Fever, uterine tenderness and offensive lochia support endometritis. Assess blood loss and haemodynamic status first; check a full blood count.

Pelvic ultrasound helps assess retained tissue, but normal postpartum appearances can be misleading. If infection is suspected, take indicated cultures and start broad-spectrum antibiotics without waiting for results.

cards.front: A low-risk woman has a newly abnormal fetal heart rate on intermittent auscultation. Begin further assessment with [___].
cards.context:
Check the maternal pulse alongside the fetal heart so the trace is not counting the mother's rate. Look for reversible causes, such as excessive uterine activity or maternal fever, while it runs.

Queensland guidance allows a return to intermittent auscultation if the trace is normal after 20 minutes.

cards.front: With the hip flexed and adducted, pushing the femur posteriorly to dislocate a located hip is the [___] manoeuvre.
cards.context:
The two manoeuvres test opposites. Barlow (push posteriorly) tests if a LOCATED hip can be dislocated — flex, adduct, push posteriorly; positive if 'clunk' as head dislocates.

Ortolani (pull anteriorly) tests if a DISLOCATED hip can be reduced — flex, abduct, lift greater trochanter forward; positive if clunk indicates reduction.

Mnemonic: Barlow Backward, Ortolani Out. Both become unreliable after 3 months as the hip stabilises in dislocation — replaced by Galeazzi sign, limited abduction, asymmetric thigh creases.

cards.front: MRI without contrast is considered safe in pregnancy; the MRI contrast agent usually avoided because of uncertain fetal effects is [___].
cards.context:
MRI without contrast does not use ionising radiation and is considered safe in pregnancy. The uncertainty sits with the contrast, not the magnet.

Iodinated CT contrast is a different agent and is described as safe when the scan is indicated.

cards.front: A woman normotensive at booking has BP 144/86 and 146/88 mmHg four hours apart at 30 weeks. Urine protein, bloods and fetal growth are normal. The diagnosis is [___].
cards.context:
New hypertension after 20 weeks, at 140 systolic and/or 90 diastolic or above, without proteinuria, organ dysfunction or fetal growth restriction, is gestational hypertension.

Keep testing: some women progress to pre-eclampsia.

cards.front: Postpartum endometritis risk is increased after caesarean section; an IV regimen for severe/systemic infection is amoxicillin + gentamicin + [___].
cards.context:
Caesarean birth increases the risk of postpartum endometritis. Fever, uterine tenderness and offensive lochia suggest infection; assess for sepsis and retained products.

SA Health recommends IV amoxicillin, gentamicin and metronidazole for severe/systemic endometritis; metronidazole forms DNA-damaging radicals in anaerobes. Allergy and local protocols determine alternatives.

[RANZCOG review](https://www.ogmagazine.org.au/21/4-21/managing-the-septic-postnatal-patient/).

cards.front: A woman with two previous miscarriages attends an early pregnancy clinic with bleeding and a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy. Which vaginal medication should be recommended until 16 weeks? [___]
cards.context:
Progesterone should be recommended when there is early pregnancy bleeding and two or more previous miscarriages. It probably increases the live birth rate.

Give micronised progesterone vaginally, 400 mg twice daily, and continue to 16 weeks.

reference.title: Miscarriage, Recurrent Miscarriage and Ectopic Pregnancy (C-Gyn 38)

cards.front: ECV is offered from 36-37 weeks for breech presentation; success rate is approximately [___]%.
cards.context:
ECV turns a breech baby head-first through abdominal pressure, usually at 36–37 weeks. Success is about 50%, and more likely after a previous vaginal birth.

After a failed attempt, discuss repeat ECV and birth options: planned caesarean, or selected vaginal breech birth with an experienced team.

[RCOG breech guidance](https://www.rcog.org.uk/for-the-public/browse-our-patient-information/breech-baby-at-the-end-of-pregnancy/).

cards.front: The increased tendency to clot after childbirth is called a [___] state.
cards.context:
Delivery-related tissue injury, venous stasis and persistent hypercoagulability raise postpartum clot risk, especially in the first six weeks. A smaller excess risk can persist beyond six weeks.

Prophylaxis depends on individual risk assessment. Australian guidance distinguishes prophylaxis until discharge, at least seven days and six weeks; Caesarean birth alone does not mandate six weeks.

cards.front: At 33 weeks, a woman develops nocturnal itching of her palms and soles without a primary rash. Non-fasting bile acids are 28 µmol/L (pregnancy reference <19); transaminases are normal. Other hepatic disease is excluded. The diagnosis is [___].
cards.context:
Bile acids establish the biochemical abnormality; normal transaminases do not exclude this pregnancy disorder.

A primary inflammatory rash would favour a dermatosis. Scratch marks alone are compatible with cholestasis.

cards.front: Lactation hormones: [___] (anterior pituitary) drives milk production; oxytocin (posterior pituitary) triggers let-down. The latter is inhibited by stress and pain.
cards.context:
Lactation runs on two complementary hormones. Prolactin (anterior pituitary) drives MILK PRODUCTION, rising with each suckling stimulus and peaking at night.

Oxytocin (posterior pituitary) drives the LET-DOWN reflex, contracting myoepithelial cells to eject stored milk.

Oxytocin release is conditioned to multiple cues but exquisitely sensitive to stress, pain, alcohol, embarrassment — these inhibit let-down even when supply is fine.

cards.front: Couvelaire uterus is blood infiltration of the myometrium from severe placental abruption, which can contribute to uterine atony and PPH; risk of [___] from disrupted decidua.
cards.context:
Couvelaire uterus (uteroplacental apoplexy) is the visual signature of severe placental abruption at caesarean — blood has dissected from retroplacental haematoma into myometrium, producing a purple, bruised uterus.

Severe abruption also releases tissue factor + procoagulants from disrupted decidua → DIC (consumptive coagulopathy: falling platelets, falling fibrinogen, raised D-dimer, prolonged INR/APTT).

Couvelaire appearance alone does not require hysterectomy; treat ongoing haemorrhage and coagulopathy. [Clinical report](https://doi.org/10.1177/87564793231224787).

cards.front: For a confirmed missed miscarriage managed medically at WNHS, the mifepristone oral dose before misoprostol is [___] mg.
cards.context: WNHS recommends mifepristone 200 mg orally, followed 24–48 hours later by misoprostol 800 micrograms vaginally, buccally or sublingually. Confirm diagnosis and arrange follow-up and emergency access.

reference.title: Miscarriage, Recurrent Miscarriage and Ectopic Pregnancy (C-Gyn 38)

cards.front: A new seizure after 20 weeks in a woman with hypertension is often heralded by brisk reflexes and [___].
cards.context:
Brisk reflexes with sustained clonus signal cerebral irritability.

They warn that a seizure may be near.

cards.front: The less variable ovarian phase is the luteal phase, which usually lasts about [___] days.
cards.context:
The luteal phase is less variable than the follicular phase and is usually about 12-14 days, but a normal range of roughly 11-17 days is recognised; it is not fixed at exactly 14 days.

Practically, subtracting 14 days from the next expected period gives an estimate of ovulation, not an exact date for every cycle. The mid-cycle rule only fits a textbook 28-day cycle.

Counting back from the next expected period is more accurate for fertility timing, ovulation detection, and luteal phase assessment in subfertility workup.

cards.front: Hypertension confirmed before pregnancy or before [___] is chronic, not gestational.
cards.context: Twenty weeks separates pre-existing chronic hypertension from gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia, which appear at or after 20 weeks.

cards.front: A chancre is the single firm, painless genital ulcer with a clean base in primary [___].
cards.context: The ulcer often comes with rubbery painless nodes. It heals even without treatment.

cards.front: A term neonate with moderate hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy is treated with therapeutic [___], started within 6 hours of birth.
cards.context: Cooling to 33-34 °C for 72 hours reduces death and disability after moderate to severe hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy. It works only if started early, so refer to a cooling centre at once.

cards.front: The only effective treatment for syphilis during pregnancy is long-acting [___].
cards.context:
A penicillin allergy is when expert advice is required. It is not a prompt to choose a substitute at the booking visit.

Contacts are still treated, and serology is repeated after the course. Neither step is how the drug is chosen.

Routine serology later in pregnancy is a screen. It does not replace treatment once infection is already confirmed.

cards.front: A dating scan, when done, is recommended at 8-14 weeks; it confirms [___], dates the pregnancy, and detects multiple gestation.
cards.context:
Australian guidance recommends a dating scan, when done, between 8+0 and 13+6 weeks. It confirms viability, dates pregnancy by CRL, and identifies multiple pregnancy/chorionicity.

Book it in this narrow window because CRL dating is more accurate than later biparietal diameter/head circumference estimates, and chorionicity is easiest to assess while membranes are clearly visible.

cards.front: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk rises about [___]-fold during pregnancy, and is even higher in the first 6 weeks after birth.
cards.context:
Pregnancy is a physiologically prothrombotic state — estrogen-driven hepatic synthesis of clotting factors (II, VII, VIII, X, fibrinogen) rises, fibrinolysis falls (raised PAI-1 and PAI-2 from placenta).

The result is a 4-5× rise in VTE risk during pregnancy itself (RCOG), and an even higher 20-80× rise in the first 6 weeks postpartum.

VTE remains a leading direct cause of maternal death in Australia. Assess every pregnant woman's risk at booking and again after each clinical change.

cards.front: Neonatal hypoglycaemia: BGL <[___] mmol/L; an asymptomatic at-risk newborn needs a BGL check at 2 hours; symptomatic → IV dextrose 10%.
cards.context:
Neonatal hypoglycaemia is BGL <2.6 mmol/L. RHW recommends the first pre-feed BGL at 2 hours for asymptomatic at-risk newborns.

A symptomatic newborn needs immediate assessment and treatment, with IV 10% dextrose when indicated.

cards.front: Safer Baby Bundle: settle to sleep on the side from [___] weeks, because going to sleep supine is linked to late stillbirth; lying supine compresses the IVC.
cards.context:
Going to sleep supine from 28 weeks is associated with late stillbirth (pooled adjusted odds ratio 2.63); either side appears equally safe.

Supine at 35-38 weeks, MRI shows IVC flow falls by about 85% and cardiac output by about 16% despite azygos collaterals: a plausible mechanism, not proven cause.

cards.front: For WNHS non-elective caesarean or higher atony risk, the slow IV oxytocin bolus is [___].
cards.context: An infusion follows the bolus. Do not substitute the ten-unit IM third-stage dose as a rapid IV bolus.

cards.front: NT >=[___] mm — a separate, fixed threshold above the >95th-centile aneuploidy-screening cutoff — is independently associated with structural anomalies including cardiac defects.
cards.context:
Increased NT (>95th centile for CRL, roughly 2.1-2.8 mm across the 11-14 week window) is a non-specific marker of fetal stress — fluid accumulation behind the fetal neck from any cause altering lymphatic drainage.

This is the aneuploidy-screening trigger. NT ≥3.5 mm is a separate, higher, fixed cutoff independently associated with cardiac and other structural anomalies, regardless of the aneuploidy screening result.

Picks up aneuploidies (T21, T18, T13, monosomy X), structural anomalies (cardiac, diaphragmatic hernia), and genetic syndromes with normal karyotype.

cards.front: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) patients with fewer than 4 cycles a year need induced withdrawal bleeds (with combined oral contraceptive pill or cyclic progestogen) to prevent endometrial [___].
cards.context:
In PCOS the persistent anovulation means unopposed estrogen drives continuous endometrial proliferation without the cyclic progesterone-driven shedding that protects the lining in normal cycles.

The fix is to recreate the missing progesterone signal. COCP delivers cyclic progestogen plus contraception (ideal in young women planning pregnancy later).

cards.front: Normal cardiotocograph (CTG): baseline [___] bpm, variability 6-25 bpm, accelerations present, no decelerations.
cards.context:
Normal CTG has four reassuring features: baseline 110-160 bpm (bradycardia <110 may be cord/heart block, tachycardia >160 may be sepsis/hypoxia).

DR C BRAVADO structures interpretation: Define Risk, Contractions, Baseline Rate, Variability, Accelerations, Decelerations, Overall.

cards.front: In NSW guidance, with regular painful contractions before 37 weeks, cervical dilatation greater than [___] distinguishes actual from threatened preterm labour.
cards.context: NSW GL2026_011 Appendix 1 distinguishes actual from threatened preterm labour at dilatation greater than 3 cm. Regular painful contractions and the full clinical assessment still matter.

cards.front: [___] is the most common cause of postpartum haemorrhage, accounting for 70-80% of cases.
cards.context:
Risk factors include: prolonged labour, overdistended uterus (multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, macrosomia), chorioamnionitis, grand multiparity, and uterine relaxants (MgSO₄, volatile anaesthetics).

The uterus should be palpated after every delivery — a boggy, poorly contracted uterus requires immediate action.

cards.front: First-line manoeuvre for shoulder dystocia is McRoberts position with [___] pressure (NOT fundal); resolves majority of cases.
cards.context:
The mechanism: hyperflexing the maternal hips onto the abdomen rotates the symphysis pubis cephalad and flattens the sacral promontory, straightening the pelvic axis and increasing the AP diameter by 1-2 cm.

Suprapubic (NOT fundal) pressure adds adduction of the anterior shoulder into the oblique diameter.

McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure resolves around 60-90% of shoulder dystocia cases — making it the highest-yield first-line manoeuvre.

cards.front: Bacterial vaginosis is a shift of the vaginal flora, normally dominated by [___], towards anaerobes such as Gardnerella.
cards.context:
BV is a shift from Lactobacillus-dominated flora towards anaerobes such as Gardnerella, Mobiluncus and Fannyhessea (formerly Atopobium).

The loss of lactobacilli raises the vaginal pH and produces the fishy amine odour and clue cells.

cards.front: Newborn blood spot screening is performed at [___] hours of life by heel prick.
cards.context:
In NSW, collect the routine heel-prick sample at 48–72 hours with consent. Do not delay the first sample until milk feeding is established.

Document feeding, early collection, prematurity and transfusions. These can affect interpretation or repeat sampling; follow the screening laboratory's advice.

Screening does not replace clinical assessment. Investigate symptoms even if the screen is normal or has not yet been collected.
